This needs to be said. It's not a good idea. It never was.

If something is impertinent or vitriolic or otherwise undesirable then the report button is called for. Otherwise, there is absolutely no reason for the downvote to exist. It is, always was and always will be a disagree button. A way to quell divergent opinions.

If we want a community with engaging discussions and not compartmentalized echo rooms, the disagree button must be abandoned.

And the upvoat is used as an agree button.

While we're stating facts, can we use that logic to remove all voating and make this 4chan with names?

Subverse owners can disable downvoats within their own subverses by setting a high CCP limit. The only price they pay is that they will not be seen in /v/all, and that's pretty fair considering that it should be a level playing field.

I don't think we should remove the downvote button, but discourage it. Having the amount and ratio of upvotes to downvotes be publicly shown is a subtly non-invasive way to make people downvote less and/or upvote more that we already have. Another measure milder and more acceptable is losing one of your own points if you downvote another person. I have often been in discussions in Reddit where I ended up arguing with one person in a chain of 10 comments and they would downvote all my comments, because of which I always downvoted them as well. This created a hostile environment, something that this would circumvent.

losing one of your own points if you downvote another person

Then your CCP would not be a direct measure of your contributions — it would effectively become a currency. The current system does not allow your downvoats given to exceed your CCP gained, which is in effect what you're suggesting without changing the CCP value itself.

Then your CCP would not be a direct measure of your contributions — it would effectively become a currency.

Which I wouldn't oppose. I am saying this as someone who has upvoted 300 comments and downvoted 3, with those 3 being racist, unintelligent and this site would be better off without their posters. The scenario I use for my justification regarding this policy is the Dirty Harty scenario where you sacrifice one of your own points for the greater good.

Right now the community is still very positive though, just like Reddit in the beginning. After a while hostility will increase and it might turn out to be very hard to do something about it then. We are probably already too late right now.
